cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is a semantic layer?
cards.answer: A shared definition tier between raw data stores and their consumers (dashboards, APIs, agents) that holds metric formulas, joins, access rules and vocabulary in one place, so a term has exactly one computable meaning.

cards.heading: How it compiles requests
cards.question: How does a semantic layer turn a consumer's request into a warehouse query?
cards.answer: Consumers request a named metric with dimensions and filters; the layer compiles that into the actual query, applying the joins and business rules the definition implies.

cards.heading: What it prevents
cards.question: What failure mode does a semantic layer prevent?
cards.answer: Definition drift — business logic forking into ad-hoc tables, dashboard-local formulas and application code that are each correct on the day written but quietly diverge afterward.

cards.heading: Why agentic access sharpens the need
cards.question: Why does agent-driven text-to-SQL make the lack of a semantic layer more dangerous, not less?
cards.answer: A model translating a question into SQL can only use rules present in the schema; when the real definition (e.g. revenue recognition timing) lives outside the tables, it produces answers that are confidently wrong and structurally plausible.

cards.heading: Rollout cost and pitfall
cards.question: What is the cost of adopting a semantic layer, and what mistake reintroduces the problem it solves?
cards.answer: It requires upfront modelling work; rolling it out one domain at a time is recommended, because enterprise-wide rollouts tend to leave legacy reports running in parallel, recreating the inconsistency the layer was meant to remove.
